clue.text: Non-British playwright authentic in his own tongue

indicators.note: the prefix non- says the British part is to be absent from the playwright's name

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht, the German dramatist

explanation.surface: A foreign dramatist is said to be genuine when speaking his native language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-' removes BR from BRECHT. The definition is fair because the answer is a German word and Brecht was German.
explanation.definitionFit: German for genuine or real, an adjective English has also borrowed.

clue.text: Burst out: "Clean up half of it"

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for clean is written from bottom to top

parts.note: clean means pure

indicators.note: only one of the two letters of the word it is taken, here its second half

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a terse instruction to tidy away half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PURE into ERUP, and 'half of' keeps the T of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano bursts out when it explodes into activity, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Eccentric rich lady bringing in University regarding piped water?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in another letter, so one sits within the other
an eccentric arrangement is an odd one, so the letters of rich lady are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd wealthy woman introduces a university to the subject of plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges the letters of rich lady, and 'bringing in' sets U among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydraulic describes things worked by liquid moving through pipes; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: End of mission to ruffle feathers, in a way

parts.note: to splash water is to ruffle its surface
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a final task of irritating somebody, upsetting them in a manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' flags that the two parts are only loosely meant: disturbing water, plus soft plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's descent into the sea concludes a space flight, as with the Apollo capsules.

clue.text: Endless reporters certain to lead to tension

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for reporters is cut off

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Reporters who never stop are bound to create a strained atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final letter; 'to lead to' means the first part comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress or strain from demands is a common synonym for this kind of force or strain.

clue.text: A second student, not entirely perceptive

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for student loses its final letter

parts.note: a tutee is someone being taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: A second pupil who is only partly sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims TUTEE to TUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick to understand, a straightforward synonym for perceptive.

clue.text: Love to search for maze

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like love
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys hunting for a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bees' wax structure of cells, or by extension any intricate network of passages like a maze.

clue.text: Schoolfellow once to hurry item in French

parts.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a school
to jet is to travel or move fast

explanation.surface: A former classmate rushes to fetch an object, described in French.
explanation.definitionFit: French for object or thing, as in objet d'art.

clue.text: Theoretically maximum support, as it were?

parts.note: something that is a maximum has no minimum, read as NO MIN
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Asks whether the greatest backing is something only in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were?' warns the first part is playful: a maximum is 'no min(imum)'.
explanation.definitionFit: In name only, as opposed to in practice or reality.

clue.text: Runs into vapours — contribution to coughing?

indicators.note: into puts the abbreviation for runs inside the word for vapours

parts.note: fog is a mist of water vapour
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone running through mist gets a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'frog in the throat' is the hoarseness that makes you clear your throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a frog in one's throat is the croakiness behind a cough.

clue.text: Covered by European articles

parts.note: European qualifies both articles; the first is un, French for a
the second article is der, German for the

explanation.surface: Something is hidden beneath pieces from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' applies to both articles: one French, one German.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beneath something means being covered by it, a positional synonym.

clue.text: Worried each soccer team after one's sent off

parts.words: soccer team after one's sent off
parts.note: a football team has eleven players; with one dismissed, ten remain

explanation.surface: Every football side is anxious after a red card.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten up, as in consumed with worry: an anxiety is eating at someone.

clue.text: Lucky to offload my problem

indicators.note: to offload is to get rid of, so the letters of my are dropped

parts.note: jammy is British slang for lucky

explanation.surface: Someone thinks themselves fortunate to unload their trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: JAMMY is everyday British slang for fortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam is being in a fix or difficulty.

clue.text: Two rents, one reduced — it keeps protests down

indicators.note: the second of the two rents is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a tear and a gash are both rents or rips

explanation.surface: Two rips, one smaller, in something that suppresses demonstrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one reduced' turns GASH into GAS after TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this irritant chemical to disperse crowds and riots.

clue.text: To be audacious is unknown in Greek god

indicators.note: in places the unknown letter inside the god's name

parts.note: Triton is a sea god, son of Poseidon
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery within a Greek deity, said to be bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for chancing one's arm, testing how far one can push one's luck.

clue.text: Measure of potential passion about a French writer

indicators.note: about means the two pieces go round the letter a

parts.note: the volt is the unit of electrical potential
ire is anger or passion

explanation.surface: An electric unit and fiery feeling surround a man of French letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets VOLTIRE around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enlightenment author of Candide.

clue.text: River mammal tailed boats for sources of warm flows

indicators.note: tailed means the creature's name has its end clipped off

parts.note: the water vole lives on riverbanks
canoes are small boats

explanation.surface: A riverside creature followed by small craft, and the origin of warm currents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' cuts VOLE to VOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lava streams pour out from these mountains, so the definition is a playful understatement.

clue.text: Tower flag flapping in fading light

indicators.note: a flapping flag moves about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banner waves atop a tower as dusk falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' rearranges TOWERFLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow left in the sky after sunset, light that is dwindling.

clue.text: Standard marks in national exam

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for marks inside the combined pieces

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Typical grades in a nationwide test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside N + ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual or regular, conforming to the norm.

clue.text: Display male's cunning history

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, the 's as is
arch means sly or knowing
the past is history

explanation.surface: A man has a crafty background.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade of troops filing past a saluting base, a military display.

clue.text: Pest is occupying shade

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit within, so the word is goes inside

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: A bug has taken over a darker tone.
explanation.definitionFit: An annoying person or thing, like a pest.

clue.text: Firm returning in former place

indicators.note: in places the turned word for firm inside the word for former

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for firm runs backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company goes back to where it used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes OC from CO; 'in' puts it in LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to find where it is or put it in position.

clue.text: Turned sad, mostly, when employed in happy plant

indicators.note: employed in means set to work inside, so the pieces go within the word for happy

parts.note: merry means happy

indicators.note: turned means the shortened word is reversed
mostly means the last letter of the word for sad is dropped

parts.note: blue means sad

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy became cheerful in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BLUE to BLU, 'Turned' makes ULB, and 'employed in' puts it in MERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree bearing dark berries, its leaves fed to silkworms.

clue.text: Military leader maintaining a lot of rank in health centre

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the leader's letters hold the other piece

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers

explanation.surface: A general keeps much of his position in a medical facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts LINE to LIN; 'maintaining' puts it in CIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where patients receive outpatient medical treatment.

clue.text: Computer program redesigned real clothes

parts.note: an app is a software application

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of real are reworked

explanation.surface: Software has remade genuine garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges REAL into AREL.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments, a formal word for dress or attire.

clue.text: Pointless climbing — a climber needs this

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters run upwards

parts.note: pointless read as no tip, without a point

explanation.surface: Mountaineering looks futile, yet one piece of kit is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns NOTIP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike hammered into rock to hold a rope, essential gear for mountaineers.

clue.text: Plant swamping untidy home one way or another

indicators.note: swamping means engulfing, so the word for plant surrounds the rest

parts.note: to sow is to plant seed

indicators.note: untidy means the letters of home are disordered

explanation.surface: A plant overruns a messy house, by some means or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' makes OMEH, and 'swamping' puts it in SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: By some means not specified, in whatever manner.

clue.text: King dodging filthy multitude

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the abbreviation for king is left out

parts.note: manky is British slang for dirty or grotty
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch avoids a dirty crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: MANKY is everyday British slang for grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Many used as a noun, as in the many, means a great number of people.

clue.text: Try to win day, after losing core of deal?

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone's love

indicators.note: losing core means the middle letter of the word day is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A trader tries to win the day after the heart of the deal is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is pine or fir timber, so the definition means made of wood; 'losing core' turns DAY into DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber, so something of deal is made of wood, a crossword-friendly sense.

clue.text: Defeated leader ousted in contest

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and ousting it removes it

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest

explanation.surface: A chief is beaten after being thrown out of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who is dismissed is beaten, as is a defeated election candidate.

clue.text: Brand new underwear

parts.note: a line is a range of products under one brand

explanation.surface: An advert for a new label of undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen once meant underclothes and bed sheets, made of flax.

clue.text: No good, then very good, over NZ tree

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Seems to rate a tree from New Zealand, first bad and then excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A small New Zealand tree, also known for writer Ngaio Marsh.

clue.text: Chase winds around submarines?

indicators.note: around means the letters of the two words are moved about

explanation.surface: Pursuit of gusts going round, perhaps underwater vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges CHASEWINDS. 'submarines' looks like vessels, but subs are long filled rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine, or sub, is a long bread roll filled like a sandwich; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Delay one in enclosure

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pigs' enclosure
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A hold-up for someone stuck in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a postponement or delay.
